name: Elastic Cloud
scope_notes: Covers Elastic Cloud (Elastic Cloud Hosted / Serverless, Elasticsearch). Covers Elastic Cloud org API keys and Elasticsearch-level credentials on ECH, Serverless and self-managed; Elasticsearch audit logging needs a qualifying subscription, and the org-level Cloud audit trail exists only on FedRAMP Moderate.

controls.name: API key expiration (Elastic Cloud)
controls.what: Key expires after a preset or date up to one year, or never.
controls.setting: Organization > API keys > Create API key > Expiration

controls.name: Roles on Cloud API keys
controls.what: Org-level, cloud resource and connected cluster roles limit what the key can do; Cloud-API-only access is default on Serverless.

controls.name: Revoke Cloud API key
controls.setting: Organization > API keys > trash icon; DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys/{api_key_id}

controls.name: xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled
controls.what: Turns off the built-in API key service for the cluster.

controls.name: Role descriptors / access on API key
controls.what: Restricts the key to given privileges and indices.

controls.name: API key expiration (Elasticsearch)
controls.setting: Kibana API keys > Create API key; expiration field

controls.name: Invalidate API keys
controls.what: Invalidated keys fail authentication; can target by owner, user or realm.

controls.name: IP filters (network security policies)
controls.what: Rejects deployment/project traffic from non-allowed IPs with 403.
controls.setting: Organization > Network security > IP filter; apply to deployments

controls.name: Organization owner / manage workload credentials (Cloud role permission)
controls.what: Only organization owners and users who can manage workload credentials can create Cloud API keys; withholding these roles blocks creation.

controls.name: manage_security privilege (cross-cluster API key creation)
controls.what: Creating or updating a cross-cluster API key needs manage_security and an Enterprise license; users without it cannot create one.

no_control.what: Service tokens cannot be given an expiry.
Built-in service accounts cannot be disabled.

controls_unknown: IP restriction for the Elastic Cloud API (api.elastic-cloud.com) used with Cloud API keys.
Whether an org can block creation of Cloud API keys with no expiry (Never).
Org-level audit log of Cloud API key creation/use outside FedRAMP Moderate.
Whether ES API keys owned by a SAML user stop working when the user is removed in the IdP.
Whether xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled can be set in ECH user settings.
Whether Cloud API key revocation affects in-flight requests.

authentication.summary: Org-owned key sent as 'Authorization: ApiKey' to api.elastic-cloud.com. Manages org, deployments and projects; on Serverless can optionally reach Elasticsearch/Kibana APIs; on ECH no Elasticsearch/Kibana access.

federation.details: Docs recommend keeping an org-owner Cloud API key to disable SSO enforcement in an emergency, implying keys work while SSO is enforced. Keys survive the creator leaving.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP filters apply to deployment/project traffic; no documented IP restriction for the Elastic Cloud API itself.

lifetime.summary: Default 3 months; up to 1 year or Never

renewal.summary: Same key reused until expiry; create a new key to rotate.

administration.summary: Organization owners and users with manage workload credentials create keys; owners see and revoke all. Max 500 active keys per org.
administration.conditions: Non-owners can assign only roles they hold.

sso.details: Elastic recommends keeping an org-owner Cloud API key to turn off SSO enforcement if the IdP fails, so keys keep working under enforced SSO.

offboard.details: The key belongs to the organization and keeps working after its creator leaves, until it expires or is revoked.

inventory.details: Organization > API keys; organization owners can view and revoke all keys in the organization.

usage.ui: Kibana (destination deployment) > [Elastic GovCloud] Organization Audit Logs dashboard; filter elastic_govcloud.org_audit.api_key.id

reads.ui: Discover on logs-elastic_govcloud.org_audit-*: filter elastic_govcloud.org_audit.api_key.id and http.request.method (every Cloud API call is logged)

token_format.notes: Opaque key; sent as Authorization: ApiKey. Response header X-Elastic-Api-Key-Expiration shows expiry.

log_sources.name: Elastic Cloud audit trail
log_sources.notes: FedRAMP Moderate only; Platinum/Enterprise; delivered to logs-elastic_govcloud.org_audit-* in a deployment you own; no backfill.

credential_id_fields.notes: API key fields mapped by the integration

anomaly_cues: Keys whose creator left the org

containment.steps: Revoke in Organization > API keys or DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys/{api_key_id}; bulk via DELETE /api/v1/users/auth/keys.
containment.notes: Also rotate any 'elastic' passwords or ES keys the Cloud key could have created.

unknown: Exact event names for key create/delete

calls.log_notes: Only on FedRAMP Moderate audit trail

calls.reveals: New 'elastic' superuser password, giving data access

credentials.name: Elasticsearch API key (personal/user API key, incl. Serverless project API keys)

authentication.summary: Base64 id:api_key sent as 'Authorization: ApiKey' to Elasticsearch/Kibana. Holds a snapshot of the creator's privileges, or the intersection with given role descriptors.

federation.details: Key is owned by a user in a realm (e.g. SAML) but works independently of IdP sessions; docs do not state behavior when the IdP user is removed.

ip_restriction.boundary: ECH/Serverless IP filters gate all deployment traffic (403); self-managed uses xpack.security.http.filter.*. Not per key.

lifetime.summary: No expiry by default (Kibana quick-create: 90 days)

administration.summary: Needs manage_api_key or manage_own_api_key; admins with manage_api_key see all keys and owners. Service can be turned off cluster-wide with xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled: false.
administration.conditions: Static setting; availability on ECH user settings not verified.

inventory.details: Kibana API Keys management page shows all users' keys to manage_api_key holders; GET /_security/api_key returns all keys.

disable.ui: Self-managed: elasticsearch.yml xpack.security.authc.api_key.enabled: false (static, restart). ECH: Edit > Elasticsearch > Manage user settings and extensions

usage.ui: ECH: deployment Edit > Elasticsearch > Manage user settings and extensions > add xpack.security.audit.enabled: true; view in monitoring deployment Discover (elastic-cloud-logs-*), filter apikey.id / authentication.type: API_KEY

reads.ui: Same audit log; filter event.action access_granted and apikey.id (access_granted is in the default include list)

token_format.notes: Encoded value is base64 of id:api_key.

log_sources.name: Elasticsearch audit log
log_sources.notes: Disabled by default; subscription-gated; on ECH requires logging and monitoring to a monitoring deployment.

anomaly_cues: Keys without expiry created by admins
Bulk _search or scroll by API key

containment.steps: DELETE /_security/api_key with ids, or by username/realm_name to kill all of a user's keys.

calls.reveals: Own keys, or all keys with read_security/manage_api_key

authentication.summary: Created on the remote cluster and stored in the local cluster keystore; authenticates only on the remote cluster interface (port 9443), not REST.

ip_restriction.boundary: Remote cluster filters (ECH) and xpack.security.remote_cluster.filter.* (self-managed); deployment IP filters.

renewal.summary: Replace key in local keystore to rotate.

administration.summary: Needs manage_security and Enterprise license; access limited exactly to the access property.

inventory.details: GET /_security/api_key returns all API keys regardless of ownership for read_security/manage_api_key holders.

disable.ui: Kibana > Roles management page > Create role / edit role: withhold manage_security cluster privilege

usage.ui: Enable audit logging on the remote (fulfilling) cluster (Manage user settings > xpack.security.audit.enabled: true); filter apikey.id

reads.ui: Remote cluster audit log: filter access_granted and apikey.id

token_format.notes: Encoded API key added to the local cluster keystore.

anomaly_cues: Cross-cluster key with broad index patterns

containment.steps: Invalidate via DELETE /_security/api_key on the remote cluster.

calls.call: GET /<index>/_search (cross-cluster search into the remote cluster)
calls.reveals: Documents in remote indices the key grants search access to
calls.log_notes: Elasticsearch audit log (access_granted is in the default include list once auditing is enabled); needs a qualifying subscription. Key identified by apikey.id.

authentication.summary: Bearer token for a service account (e.g. elastic/fleet-server, elastic/kibana) with fixed privileges.

federation.details: Service-only credential, not usable by people.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only via deployment IP filters / HTTP filters; not per token.

renewal.summary: Create new token and delete old one.

administration.summary: manage_service_account for built-in accounts; manage_security for user-managed accounts. Built-in accounts are always enabled.
administration.conditions: User-managed service accounts appear in current API reference with an enabled flag.

offboard.details: Service accounts are for external services, not individual users.

inventory.details: Get service accounts API, then get service account credentials API per account (includes file-backed tokens).

usage.ui: Enable audit logging (xpack.security.audit.enabled: true); filter authentication.token.name

reads.ui: Audit log: filter access_granted and authentication.token.name

token_format.notes: Bearer token; secret part at least 22 chars.

anomaly_cues: Service token used from outside Fleet/Kibana hosts

containment.steps: Delete the token via API; file-backed tokens need the service_tokens file edited.
containment.notes: Index-backed token cache clears automatically when the security index changes (for example, a token delete); file-backed cache clears on file change. No derived tokens.

calls.reveals: Documents in indices covered by the service account's fixed privileges
calls.log_notes: Elasticsearch audit log (access_granted is in the default include list once auditing is enabled); needs a qualifying subscription. Token identified by authentication.token.name.
